nodes.title: Sessions use one long-lived access token and the API has no refresh tokens.
nodes.content:
Sessions use one long-lived access token and the API has no refresh tokens.
The API issues a single access token that is valid for one week and has no refresh endpoint. A client that needs a new token logs in again.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: Security review SR-2025-14 of the pilot found that a stored refresh token let a stolen browser profile keep access for months. The team chose a one-week access token and no refresh token, so a stolen token expires on its own. Invented for this demo.
nodes.justification: Security review SR-2025-14 of the pilot found that a stored refresh token let a stolen browser profile keep access for months. The team chose a one-week access token and no refresh token, so a stolen token expires on its own. Invented for this demo.

nodes.title: Password reset links stay valid for 30 minutes.
nodes.content:
Password reset links stay valid for 30 minutes.
The API has no password reset flow yet. This fixes the rule for when it is built: a reset link works once and expires 30 minutes after it is sent.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: Support tickets showed that users open a reset mail within 10 minutes. A link that lives 30 minutes covers slow mail delivery without leaving a long-lived link in an inbox. Invented for this demo.
nodes.justification: Support tickets showed that users open a reset mail within 10 minutes. A link that lives 30 minutes covers slow mail delivery without leaving a long-lived link in an inbox. Invented for this demo.

nodes.title: Access tokens expire one week after issue.
nodes.content:
Access tokens get an exp claim of 60 * 24 * 7 minutes after creation. There is no refresh token; a new token is issued on login, registration and every GET or PUT of the current user.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:12

nodes.title: Login returns the same 400 error for an unknown email and a wrong password.
nodes.content:
The login route builds one wrong_login_error and raises it both when the email is not found and when check_password fails. Login is by email, not username.
Source: app/app/api/routes/authentication.py:28

nodes.title: A separate per-user salt is stored in its own column and prepended to the password before hashing.
nodes.content:
change_password generates a new bcrypt salt, stores it in users.salt, and hashes salt + password. check_password must use the same concatenation, so dropping or reordering the salt breaks every existing login.
Source: app/app/models/domain/users.py:24
nodes.context: UserInDB in app/app/models/domain/users.py and users.salt column in the migration.

nodes.title: Registering with a username or email that is already taken is answered with HTTP 400.
nodes.content:
The register route checks the username first and the email second. Each taken value raises a 400 error with its own message from the strings module.
Source: app/app/api/routes/authentication.py:70

nodes.title: The JWT payload identifies the user by username, not by numeric id.
nodes.content:
The token content is only the username; the current user is loaded with get_user_by_username. Because usernames can be changed via PUT /user, a rename makes older tokens resolve to no user (403).
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:29
nodes.context: Token payload in app/app/services/jwt.py and lookup in app/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py.

nodes.title: Every access token carries the fixed subject claim access.
nodes.content:
The token payload holds the username plus an expiry and the subject value access, which is a constant in the JWT service.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:10

nodes.title: Tokens travel only in the Authorization header and never in cookies.
nodes.content:
Tokens travel only in the Authorization header and never in cookies.
The API reads the token from the Authorization header. It does not set or read any cookie.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: Cookie transport would need CSRF protection that this API does not have (ADR-5). Invented for this demo.
nodes.justification: Cookie transport would need CSRF protection that this API does not have (ADR-5). Invented for this demo.

nodes.title: The Authorization header scheme defaults to the word Token instead of Bearer.
nodes.content:
AppSettings sets jwt_token_prefix to "Token". Clients must send "Authorization: Token <jwt>"; the setting is configurable per environment.
Source: app/app/core/settings/app.py:29

nodes.title: Only an article's author, matched by username, may modify the article.
nodes.content:
The service compares the article author's username with the current user's username. Other users get a refusal.
Source: app/app/services/articles.py:23

nodes.title: Only the article author may update or delete an article, checked by username equality.
nodes.content:
check_user_can_modify_article compares the article author's username with the current user's username. The PUT and DELETE article routes depend on check_article_modification_permissions, which uses it.
Source: app/app/services/articles.py:23

nodes.title: Each user gets a random salt created with bcrypt.gensalt.
nodes.content:
A helper returns a fresh bcrypt salt as text. The user row stores the salt next to the hashed password.
Source: app/app/services/security.py:8

nodes.title: bcrypt keeps the default passlib work factor.
nodes.content:
bcrypt keeps the default passlib work factor.
No custom rounds value is set on the password context, so passlib's default applies.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: Load test LT-9 put the login endpoint at a p95 of 240 ms with the default factor. One step higher pushed it past the 300 ms login budget. Invented for this demo.
nodes.justification: Load test LT-9 put the login endpoint at a p95 of 240 ms with the default factor. One step higher pushed it past the 300 ms login budget. Invented for this demo.

nodes.title: Deleting a user keeps their articles and sets author_id to NULL.
nodes.content:
articles.author_id references users.id with ondelete SET NULL, while comments, favorites and follows cascade. Orphaned articles therefore have no author.
Source: app/app/db/migrations/versions/fdf8821871d7_main_tables.py:108
nodes.context: Articles table foreign key in the initial migration.

nodes.title: JWT access tokens are signed with the symmetric HS256 algorithm.
nodes.content:
The JWT service signs and verifies every access token with HS256 using the app secret_key. Decoding accepts only this one algorithm, so changing it invalidates all issued tokens.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:11

nodes.title: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt through a passlib CryptContext.
nodes.content:
A module-level CryptContext uses the bcrypt scheme with deprecated="auto". verify_password and get_password_hash both go through this context.
Source: app/app/services/security.py:4

nodes.title: The Authorization header is parsed by splitting on a single space and rejected with 403 if the prefix does not match.
nodes.content:
The header value must split into exactly two parts on one space, and the first part must equal settings.jwt_token_prefix. Any other shape, or an invalid token or unknown user, returns 403 rather than 401.
Source: app/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py:51

nodes.title: Access tokens are signed with the HS256 algorithm using one shared secret key.
nodes.content:
Tokens are JWTs signed and verified with HS256. The secret comes from the application settings.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:11

nodes.title: updated_at is maintained by a PostgreSQL BEFORE UPDATE trigger, not by application code.
nodes.content:
The migration creates a plpgsql function that sets NEW.updated_at = now(), and attaches it to users, articles and commentaries. Repositories read updated_at back from the database after an update.
Source: app/app/db/migrations/versions/fdf8821871d7_main_tables.py:27

nodes.title: Favoriting an article sends no notification to its author.
nodes.content:
Favoriting an article sends no notification to its author.
Adding a favorite writes a database row and nothing else. No message is sent to the author.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: Product decision PD-8 puts all notifications out of scope until the 2027 roadmap. Invented for this demo.
nodes.justification: Product decision PD-8 puts all notifications out of scope until the 2027 roadmap. Invented for this demo.

nodes.title: Updating an article title regenerates its slug, so the article URL changes.
nodes.content:
The update route computes a new slug from the new title when one is given and passes it to update_article. Unlike create, it does not check whether the new slug already exists.
Source: app/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:100

nodes.title: Creating a tag that already exists is ignored by the insert statement.
nodes.content:
The tag insert uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so saving an article with a known tag adds no new tag row.
Source: app/app/db/queries/sql/tags.sql:9

nodes.title: Queries are hand-written SQL files, not generated by an ORM.
nodes.content:
Queries are hand-written SQL files, not generated by an ORM.
Every query lives in a SQL file that the repositories call by name.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: The DBA team reviews every query. A SQL file can be reviewed in a pull request and ORM output cannot (ADR-4). Invented for this demo.
nodes.justification: The DBA team reviews every query. A SQL file can be reviewed in a pull request and ORM output cannot (ADR-4). Invented for this demo.

nodes.title: JWT access tokens are signed with the symmetric HS256 algorithm.
nodes.content:
The JWT service signs and verifies every access token with HS256 using the app secret_key. Decoding accepts only this one algorithm, so changing it invalidates all issued tokens.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:11

nodes.title: A separate per-user salt is stored in its own column and prepended to the password before hashing.
nodes.content:
change_password generates a new bcrypt salt, stores it in users.salt, and hashes salt + password. check_password must use the same concatenation, so dropping or reordering the salt breaks every existing login.
Source: app/app/models/domain/users.py:24
nodes.context: UserInDB in app/app/models/domain/users.py and users.salt column in the migration.

nodes.title: The JWT payload identifies the user by username, not by numeric id.
nodes.content:
The token content is only the username; the current user is loaded with get_user_by_username. Because usernames can be changed via PUT /user, a rename makes older tokens resolve to no user (403).
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:29
nodes.context: Token payload in app/app/services/jwt.py and lookup in app/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py.

nodes.title: PostgreSQL is the data store and MongoDB was not chosen.
nodes.content:
PostgreSQL is the data store and MongoDB was not chosen.
Articles, tags and favorites are stored in PostgreSQL tables joined by foreign keys.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: The data is relational, and the DBA team supports only PostgreSQL (ADR-3). Invented for this demo.
nodes.justification: The data is relational, and the DBA team supports only PostgreSQL (ADR-3). Invented for this demo.

nodes.title: Request validation failures return HTTP 422 with an errors list of the validator's error objects.
nodes.content:
A separate handler catches validation errors and answers with the validator's own error list, not the single detail string used for other HTTP errors.
Source: app/app/api/errors/validation_error.py:17

nodes.title: updated_at is maintained by a PostgreSQL BEFORE UPDATE trigger, not by application code.
nodes.content:
The migration creates a plpgsql function that sets NEW.updated_at = now(), and attaches it to users, articles and commentaries. Repositories read updated_at back from the database after an update.
Source: app/app/db/migrations/versions/fdf8821871d7_main_tables.py:27

nodes.title: Article lists default to 20 items with limit at least 1 and no upper bound.
nodes.content:
ArticlesFilters sets limit to DEFAULT_ARTICLES_LIMIT (20) with ge=1 and offset default 0 with ge=0. No maximum is enforced on limit.
Source: app/app/models/schemas/articles.py:42

nodes.title: Creating an article whose generated slug already exists is refused with HTTP 400.
nodes.content:
The create route builds the slug from the title and checks whether an article with that slug exists. If it does, the route raises a 400 error and does not add a numeric suffix.
Source: app/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:65

nodes.title: Tokens travel only in the Authorization header and never in cookies.
nodes.content:
Tokens travel only in the Authorization header and never in cookies.
The API reads the token from the Authorization header. It does not set or read any cookie.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: Cookie transport would need CSRF protection that this API does not have (ADR-5). Invented for this demo.
nodes.justification: Cookie transport would need CSRF protection that this API does not have (ADR-5). Invented for this demo.

nodes.title: The article list defaults to 20 items per page.
nodes.content:
The article list defaults to 20 items per page.
The default limit of the article list is 20 items.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: Design review DR-31 found that the mobile list screen fits 20 rows without scrolling. Invented for this demo.
nodes.justification: Design review DR-31 found that the mobile list screen fits 20 rows without scrolling. Invented for this demo.

nodes.title: Login returns the same 400 error for an unknown email and a wrong password.
nodes.content:
The login route builds one wrong_login_error and raises it both when the email is not found and when check_password fails. Login is by email, not username.
Source: app/app/api/routes/authentication.py:28

nodes.title: The fancyhash package is not used for password hashing because of its licence.
nodes.content:
The fancyhash package is not used for password hashing because of its licence.
Password hashing stays on passlib with bcrypt. The fancyhash package was evaluated and rejected.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: The licence of fancyhash has a network-use clause that is not compatible with distributing the API. Passlib with bcrypt was kept. Invented for this demo.
nodes.justification: The licence of fancyhash has a network-use clause that is not compatible with distributing the API. Passlib with bcrypt was kept. Invented for this demo.

nodes.title: bcrypt keeps the default passlib work factor.
nodes.content:
bcrypt keeps the default passlib work factor.
No custom rounds value is set on the password context, so passlib's default applies.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: Load test LT-9 put the login endpoint at a p95 of 240 ms with the default factor. One step higher pushed it past the 300 ms login budget. Invented for this demo.
nodes.justification: Load test LT-9 put the login endpoint at a p95 of 240 ms with the default factor. One step higher pushed it past the 300 ms login budget. Invented for this demo.

nodes.title: articlesCount in list responses is the length of the returned page, not the total number of matches.
nodes.content:
list_articles sets articles_count to len(articles) after applying limit and offset. No separate count query is run.
Source: app/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:49

nodes.title: The article slug is a unique, indexed column and is the public key for articles.
nodes.content:
articles.slug is Text, unique, not null and indexed. Routes, favorites, tags and comments look articles up by slug rather than by id.
Source: app/app/db/migrations/versions/fdf8821871d7_main_tables.py:103
nodes.context: Articles table in the initial migration.

nodes.title: Access tokens expire one week after issue.
nodes.content:
Access tokens get an exp claim of 60 * 24 * 7 minutes after creation. There is no refresh token; a new token is issued on login, registration and every GET or PUT of the current user.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:12

nodes.title: Database queries are raw SQL files loaded with aiosql for asyncpg, not an ORM.
nodes.content:
queries.py loads every .sql file in the sql folder through aiosql with the asyncpg adapter. Only filter_articles builds SQL dynamically with pypika.
Source: app/app/db/queries/queries.py:5

nodes.title: Registering with a username or email that is already taken is answered with HTTP 400.
nodes.content:
The register route checks the username first and the email second. Each taken value raises a 400 error with its own message from the strings module.
Source: app/app/api/routes/authentication.py:70

nodes.title: Each user gets a random salt created with bcrypt.gensalt.
nodes.content:
A helper returns a fresh bcrypt salt as text. The user row stores the salt next to the hashed password.
Source: app/app/services/security.py:8

nodes.title: Every access token carries the fixed subject claim access.
nodes.content:
The token payload holds the username plus an expiry and the subject value access, which is a constant in the JWT service.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:10

nodes.title: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt through a passlib CryptContext.
nodes.content:
A module-level CryptContext uses the bcrypt scheme with deprecated="auto". verify_password and get_password_hash both go through this context.
Source: app/app/services/security.py:4

nodes.title: An article slug is derived from its title with python-slugify.
nodes.content:
get_slug_for_article returns slugify(title) with no suffix or id. Creating an article whose title slugifies to an existing slug fails with 400 ARTICLE_ALREADY_EXISTS.
Source: app/app/services/articles.py:19
nodes.context: Slug generation in app/app/services/articles.py, used by app/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py.

nodes.title: The Authorization header scheme defaults to the word Token instead of Bearer.
nodes.content:
AppSettings sets jwt_token_prefix to "Token". Clients must send "Authorization: Token <jwt>"; the setting is configurable per environment.
Source: app/app/core/settings/app.py:29

nodes.title: Only an article's author, matched by username, may modify the article.
nodes.content:
The service compares the article author's username with the current user's username. Other users get a refusal.
Source: app/app/services/articles.py:23

nodes.title: PostgreSQL
nodes.content: PostgreSQL

nodes.title: The asyncpg connection pool is fixed at 10 connections by default (min equals max).
nodes.content:
AppSettings defaults both min_connection_count and max_connection_count to 10, and connect_to_db passes them as min_size and max_size.
Source: app/app/core/settings/app.py:23
nodes.context: Settings in app/app/core/settings/app.py and pool creation in app/app/db/events.py.

nodes.title: Cross-origin calls are allowed from the origins in allowed_hosts, which default to every origin.
nodes.content:
The CORS middleware reads allowed_hosts from the settings. The default list holds a single wildcard entry.
Source: app/app/core/settings/app.py:31

nodes.title: All domain models expose camelCase JSON field names through a pydantic alias generator.
nodes.content:
RWModel converts snake_case field names to camelCase aliases and also allows population by field name. Datetimes are encoded as UTC ISO strings ending in Z.
Source: app/app/models/domain/rwmodel.py:21

nodes.title: The Authorization header is parsed by splitting on a single space and rejected with 403 if the prefix does not match.
nodes.content:
The header value must split into exactly two parts on one space, and the first part must equal settings.jwt_token_prefix. Any other shape, or an invalid token or unknown user, returns 403 rather than 401.
Source: app/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py:51

nodes.title: Access tokens are signed with the HS256 algorithm using one shared secret key.
nodes.content:
Tokens are JWTs signed and verified with HS256. The secret comes from the application settings.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:11

nodes.title: The database pool is fixed at 10 connections through min_connection_count and max_connection_count.
nodes.content:
Both pool bounds default to 10 in the application settings, and the pool is created with those two values at start-up.
Source: app/app/core/settings/app.py:22

nodes.title: The article slug is a unique, indexed column and is the public key for articles.
nodes.content:
articles.slug is Text, unique, not null and indexed. Routes, favorites, tags and comments look articles up by slug rather than by id.

nodes.title: Creating a tag that already exists is ignored by the insert statement.
nodes.content:
The tag insert uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so saving an article with a known tag adds no new tag row.
Source: app/app/db/queries/sql/tags.sql:9

nodes.title: PostgreSQL is the data store and MongoDB was not chosen.
nodes.content:
PostgreSQL is the data store and MongoDB was not chosen.
Articles, tags and favorites are stored in PostgreSQL tables joined by foreign keys.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: The data is relational, and the DBA team supports only PostgreSQL (ADR-3). Invented for this demo.
nodes.justification: The data is relational, and the DBA team supports only PostgreSQL (ADR-3). Invented for this demo.

nodes.title: The article list defaults to 20 items per page.
nodes.content:
The article list defaults to 20 items per page.
The default limit of the article list is 20 items.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: Design review DR-31 found that the mobile list screen fits 20 rows without scrolling. Invented for this demo.
nodes.justification: Design review DR-31 found that the mobile list screen fits 20 rows without scrolling. Invented for this demo.

nodes.title: Article lists default to 20 items with limit at least 1 and no upper bound.
nodes.content:
ArticlesFilters sets limit to DEFAULT_ARTICLES_LIMIT (20) with ge=1 and offset default 0 with ge=0. No maximum is enforced on limit.
Source: app/app/models/schemas/articles.py:42

nodes.title: Deleted articles and comments are removed from the database, with no soft-delete flag.
nodes.content:
Deleted articles and comments are removed from the database, with no soft-delete flag.
Deleting an article or a comment runs a SQL DELETE. No deleted_at column exists.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: Legal review LR-77 requires that content its author deleted is gone from live storage within 24 hours. A deleted_at column was rejected because the rows would stay in the table. Invented for this demo.
nodes.justification: Legal review LR-77 requires that content its author deleted is gone from live storage within 24 hours. A deleted_at column was rejected because the rows would stay in the table. Invented for this demo.

nodes.title: An article slug is derived from its title with python-slugify.
nodes.content:
get_slug_for_article returns slugify(title) with no suffix or id. Creating an article whose title slugifies to an existing slug fails with 400 ARTICLE_ALREADY_EXISTS.
Source: app/app/services/articles.py:19
nodes.context: Slug generation in app/app/services/articles.py, used by app/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py.

nodes.title: Updating an article title regenerates its slug, so the article URL changes.
nodes.content:
The update route computes a new slug from the new title when one is given and passes it to update_article. Unlike create, it does not check whether the new slug already exists.
Source: app/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:100

nodes.title: articlesCount in list responses is the length of the returned page, not the total number of matches.
nodes.content:
list_articles sets articles_count to len(articles) after applying limit and offset. No separate count query is run.
Source: app/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:49

nodes.title: Deleting a user keeps their articles and sets author_id to NULL.
nodes.content:
articles.author_id references users.id with ondelete SET NULL, while comments, favorites and follows cascade. Orphaned articles therefore have no author.
Source: app/app/db/migrations/versions/fdf8821871d7_main_tables.py:108
nodes.context: Articles table foreign key in the initial migration.

nodes.title: Database queries are raw SQL files loaded with aiosql for asyncpg, not an ORM.
nodes.content:
queries.py loads every .sql file in the sql folder through aiosql with the asyncpg adapter. Only filter_articles builds SQL dynamically with pypika.
Source: app/app/db/queries/queries.py:5

nodes.title: Queries are hand-written SQL files, not generated by an ORM.
nodes.content:
Queries are hand-written SQL files, not generated by an ORM.
Every query lives in a SQL file that the repositories call by name.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: The DBA team reviews every query. A SQL file can be reviewed in a pull request and ORM output cannot (ADR-4). Invented for this demo.
nodes.justification: The DBA team reviews every query. A SQL file can be reviewed in a pull request and ORM output cannot (ADR-4). Invented for this demo.

nodes.title: Only the article author may update or delete an article, checked by username equality.
nodes.content:
check_user_can_modify_article compares the article author's username with the current user's username. The PUT and DELETE article routes depend on check_article_modification_permissions, which uses it.
Source: app/app/services/articles.py:23

nodes.title: Creating an article whose generated slug already exists is refused with HTTP 400.
nodes.content:
The create route builds the slug from the title and checks whether an article with that slug exists. If it does, the route raises a 400 error and does not add a numeric suffix.
Source: app/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:65

nodes.title: Only an article's author, matched by username, may modify the article.
nodes.content:
The service compares the article author's username with the current user's username. Other users get a refusal.
Source: app/app/services/articles.py:23

nodes.title: Favoriting an article sends no notification to its author.
nodes.content:
Favoriting an article sends no notification to its author.
Adding a favorite writes a database row and nothing else. No message is sent to the author.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: Product decision PD-8 puts all notifications out of scope until the 2027 roadmap. Invented for this demo.
nodes.justification: Product decision PD-8 puts all notifications out of scope until the 2027 roadmap. Invented for this demo.

nodes.title: Tokens travel only in the Authorization header and never in cookies.
nodes.content:
Tokens travel only in the Authorization header and never in cookies.
The API reads the token from the Authorization header. It does not set or read any cookie.

nodes.content:
The fancyhash package is not used for password hashing because of its licence.
Password hashing stays on passlib with bcrypt. The fancyhash package was evaluated and rejected.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: The licence of fancyhash has a network-use clause that is not compatible with distributing the API. Passlib with bcrypt was kept. Invented for this demo.
nodes.justification: The licence of fancyhash has a network-use clause that is not compatible with distributing the API. Passlib with bcrypt was kept. Invented for this demo.

nodes.title: bcrypt keeps the default passlib work factor.
nodes.content:
bcrypt keeps the default passlib work factor.
No custom rounds value is set on the password context, so passlib's default applies.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: Load test LT-9 put the login endpoint at a p95 of 240 ms with the default factor. One step higher pushed it past the 300 ms login budget. Invented for this demo.
nodes.justification: Load test LT-9 put the login endpoint at a p95 of 240 ms with the default factor. One step higher pushed it past the 300 ms login budget. Invented for this demo.

nodes.title: Cross-origin calls are allowed from the origins in allowed_hosts, which default to every origin.
nodes.content:
The CORS middleware reads allowed_hosts from the settings. The default list holds a single wildcard entry.
Source: app/app/core/settings/app.py:31

nodes.title: Sessions use one long-lived access token and the API has no refresh tokens.
nodes.content:
Sessions use one long-lived access token and the API has no refresh tokens.
The API issues a single access token that is valid for one week and has no refresh endpoint. A client that needs a new token logs in again.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: Security review SR-2025-14 of the pilot found that a stored refresh token let a stolen browser profile keep access for months. The team chose a one-week access token and no refresh token, so a stolen token expires on its own. Invented for this demo.
nodes.justification: Security review SR-2025-14 of the pilot found that a stored refresh token let a stolen browser profile keep access for months. The team chose a one-week access token and no refresh token, so a stolen token expires on its own. Invented for this demo.

nodes.title: Request validation failures return HTTP 422 with an errors list of the validator's error objects.
nodes.content:
A separate handler catches validation errors and answers with the validator's own error list, not the single detail string used for other HTTP errors.
Source: app/app/api/errors/validation_error.py:17

nodes.title: The Authorization header is parsed by splitting on a single space and rejected with 403 if the prefix does not match.
nodes.content:
The header value must split into exactly two parts on one space, and the first part must equal settings.jwt_token_prefix. Any other shape, or an invalid token or unknown user, returns 403 rather than 401.
Source: app/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py:51

nodes.title: The Authorization header scheme defaults to the word Token instead of Bearer.
nodes.content:
AppSettings sets jwt_token_prefix to "Token". Clients must send "Authorization: Token <jwt>"; the setting is configurable per environment.
Source: app/app/core/settings/app.py:29

nodes.title: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt through a passlib CryptContext.
nodes.content:
A module-level CryptContext uses the bcrypt scheme with deprecated="auto". verify_password and get_password_hash both go through this context.
Source: app/app/services/security.py:4

nodes.title: Access tokens are signed with the HS256 algorithm using one shared secret key.
nodes.content:
Tokens are JWTs signed and verified with HS256. The secret comes from the application settings.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:11

nodes.title: Every access token carries the fixed subject claim access.
nodes.content:
The token payload holds the username plus an expiry and the subject value access, which is a constant in the JWT service.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:10

nodes.title: JWT access tokens are signed with the symmetric HS256 algorithm.
nodes.content:
The JWT service signs and verifies every access token with HS256 using the app secret_key. Decoding accepts only this one algorithm, so changing it invalidates all issued tokens.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:11

nodes.title: Registering with a username or email that is already taken is answered with HTTP 400.
nodes.content:
The register route checks the username first and the email second. Each taken value raises a 400 error with its own message from the strings module.
Source: app/app/api/routes/authentication.py:70

nodes.title: Access tokens expire one week after issue.
nodes.content:
Access tokens get an exp claim of 60 * 24 * 7 minutes after creation. There is no refresh token; a new token is issued on login, registration and every GET or PUT of the current user.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:12

nodes.title: Password reset links stay valid for 30 minutes.
nodes.content:
Password reset links stay valid for 30 minutes.
The API has no password reset flow yet. This fixes the rule for when it is built: a reset link works once and expires 30 minutes after it is sent.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: Support tickets showed that users open a reset mail within 10 minutes. A link that lives 30 minutes covers slow mail delivery without leaving a long-lived link in an inbox. Invented for this demo.
nodes.justification: Support tickets showed that users open a reset mail within 10 minutes. A link that lives 30 minutes covers slow mail delivery without leaving a long-lived link in an inbox. Invented for this demo.

nodes.title: The JWT payload identifies the user by username, not by numeric id.
nodes.content:
The token content is only the username; the current user is loaded with get_user_by_username. Because usernames can be changed via PUT /user, a rename makes older tokens resolve to no user (403).
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:29

nodes.title: A separate per-user salt is stored in its own column and prepended to the password before hashing.
nodes.content:
change_password generates a new bcrypt salt, stores it in users.salt, and hashes salt + password. check_password must use the same concatenation, so dropping or reordering the salt breaks every existing login.
Source: app/app/models/domain/users.py:24

nodes.title: Login returns the same 400 error for an unknown email and a wrong password.
nodes.content:
The login route builds one wrong_login_error and raises it both when the email is not found and when check_password fails. Login is by email, not username.
